[[Category:Artificial neural network]]
An '''artificial neuron''' is an elementary computational unit in an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]], loosely inspired by [[biological neuron]]s.<ref>{{#cite:Q3074}}</ref>

== Mathematical representation ==

{{#content:Q3075}}

== Layer composition ==

Let $l$ be a '''layer of artificial neurons''' receiving the same '''input vector''' $\vec x=(x_i)=(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_m)$.

Then the '''layer pre-activation vector'''

$$
\vec z^{(l)}=(z_1,z_2,\dots,z_n)
$$

and the '''layer activation vector'''

$$
\vec a^{(l)}=(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n)=(f(z_1),f(z_2),\dots,f(z_n)) =f(\vec z^{(l)})
$$

since the '''[[activation function]]''' $f$ is component-wise by definition.

=== Basic form ===

When

$$
z_j = \sum_{i=1}^{m} w_{j,i} x_i + b_j
$$

then

$$
\vec z^{(l)}=\mathbf{W}\vec x + \vec b \\
\vec a^{(l)}=f(\vec z^{(l)})=f(\mathbf{W}\vec x + \vec b)
$$

where $\mathbf{W}$ is an $n \times m$ dimensioned matrix, known as the '''weight matrix''' of layer $l$, satisfying

$$
\mathbf{W}(j,i)=w_{j,i}
$$

and $\vec b=(b_j) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is known as the '''bias vector''' of layer $l$.

i.e.,

$$
\vec a^{(l)} =
f \left(
\begin{pmatrix}
w_{0,0} & w_{0,1} & \cdots & w_{0,m} \\
w_{1,0} & w_{1,1} & \cdots & w_{1,m} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
w_{n,0} & w_{n,1} & \cdots & w_{n,m}
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
x_1 \\
x_2 \\
\vdots \\
x_m
\end{pmatrix}
+
\begin{pmatrix}
b_0 \\
b_1 \\
\vdots \\
b_n
\end{pmatrix}^\mathrm{T}
\right)
$$

== Training ==

During training of an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]], weights and bias of each artificial neuron are adjusted to achieve desired output behaviour.<ref>{{#cite:Q3074}}</ref>
